asvs_5_0.structure: 17 chapters, ~350 requirements; renumbered; new standalone chapters V3 Web Frontend Security, V9 Self-contained Tokens, V10 OAuth/OIDC; V5 split into V1/V2; crypto split into application (V11) and transport (V12)
asvs_5_0.changes_vs_4_0: Levels rebalanced: L1 ~20% of requirements (lighter, 'minimum'), L2 cumulative ~70%, L3 all; deduplicated and pruned untestable requirements; guidance moved out of requirement text; added post-quantum planning, AI/security-decision documentation; removed legacy items (32-bit salt, Unicode password rules); compliance re-evaluation required
asvs_5_0.how_to_use: Adopt 5.0 IDs as the canonical requirement key in the client library; build a 4.0.3 to 5.0 crosswalk before migrating Jira requirement sets; use L2 as default target for internet-facing apps; load ASVS JSON into LLM/MCP grounding

market_trends_2025_2026: Secure-by-design mandates: CISA Secure by Design pledge (2024) and EU Cyber Resilience Act obligations (reporting from Sept 2026, full application Dec 2027) push requirement evidence from optional to auditable; SAMM published CRA guidance Feb 2026, SAMMY and Aptori sell CRA tracking.
ASVS 5.0 (May 2025) is the new baseline; renumbering forces every library and Jira requirement set to be re-mapped. Vendors are uneven in shipping 5.0 content; verify before buying.

AI-generated requirements moved from experiment to product: Seezo, Prime Security, Remy (design-stage review), IriusRisk Jeff/Bex, ThreatModeler Nexus agents (GA June 2026), Devici agents. Deterministic vendors (SD Elements) position as the policy layer that constrains AI coding agents rather than as LLM generators.

MCP is the new integration surface: SD Elements MCP (Feb 2026), Devici MCP, IriusRisk MCP, ThreatModeler Nexus MCP, SAMMY MCP connector, community ASVS MCP server (Oct 2025). Requirements are delivered inside Copilot/Cursor/Claude sessions instead of documents.

Shift from documents to policy-as-code: requirements verified by scanner policies (GitLab MR approval policies, Jit plans, ArmorCode/ASPM SLAs) and by SAST validation of requirements (SD Elements + ZeroPath).

Consolidation: Invicti acquired Kondukto (Aug 2025); tromzo.com now redirects to Checkmarx (unconfirmed); Security Compass bundles SD Elements with Devici, Kontra, AppSec Modules and adds Agentic AI Workflow as a paid upgrade.

OWASP Top 10:2025 (Nov 2025) elevates supply chain and exceptional-condition handling; OWASP Secure by Design Framework (v0.5, Aug 2025) and AISVS/AI Exchange extend requirement sources to design and AI.

top_3_recommended_contenders.reasoning: Only mature system of record for deterministic, audit-ready requirements with 100+ framework mappings, Jira/ADO traceability, SAST validation and an MCP layer for AI agents; federal on-prem editions. Cost from ~$75K/yr and survey overhead are the trade-offs.

Best when requirements should derive from an architecture-level threat model; countermeasure libraries cover ASVS/NIST/PCI/ISO, strong Jira/ADO/ServiceNow round-trip, on-prem available, free Community Edition for pilots, Jeff/Bex AI GA.

Broadest control library (3,500+ requirements, 180+ frameworks) with BYO-AI agents and MCP, GA June 2026; strongest for cloud/OT/product-security clients and FedRAMP-bound work. Requirements remain model-bound and pricing is opaque.

category_notes.best_oss_free_pick: OWASP ASVS 5.0 data + OpenCRE crosswalks + Codific SAMMY free tier for program tracking; SecurityRAT only for a throwaway ASVS-to-Jira pilot given its maintenance state. For AI grounding, the community ASVS MCP server (clintcan) is usable but unofficial.
